title: GH#33054: fix(oauth-pool): show OAuth URL and read auth code from terminal in console sessions
body:
Resolves #33054

## Summary

In console-only sessions, `model-accounts-pool add` did not print the OAuth URL, and the pasted authorization code was lost. This PR fixes it at the root:

- `open_browser()` (`.agents/scripts/oauth-pool-helper.sh`) always prints the URL first. It skips launchers when there is no graphical display (Linux without `DISPLAY`/`WAYLAND_DISPLAY`/WSL), so `xdg-open` cannot fall back to lynx/w3m. Launchers now run with detached stdio (`</dev/null >/dev/null 2>&1`), so they can no longer consume the terminal's stdin or write into the `$(...)` capture pipe.
- New `oauth_prompt_read()` prompts and reads on `/dev/tty` when a controlling terminal exists and falls back to stderr/stdin for headless use. It is used by `_add_prompt_email`, `_add_read_auth_code` and `cmd_add_google` (`.agents/scripts/oauth-pool-add.sh`).

## Reproducer

With a fake `xdg-open` in PATH that prints to stdout and runs `cat >/dev/null`, pipe `THECODE#NONCE` into `_cmd_add_pkce_authorize`:

- before: `[ERROR] No authorization code provided`, exit 1 (with or without `DISPLAY`);
- after: the URL is printed, the prompt is shown and the result is `rc=0 code=[THECODE]` in both GUI and console modes. Under a pty (`script -qec`) the prompt waits on `/dev/tty` as expected.

## Verification

- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/oauth-pool-helper.sh .agents/scripts/oauth-pool-add.sh`: clean
- `bash tests/test-oauth-pool-helper.sh`: 13 passed, 0 failed
- Pre-commit quality validation: passed

## Regression Evidence

This fix needs an interactive controlling terminal (`/dev/tty`) and a real browser launcher (`xdg-open`/`open`/`wslview`). CI runners have no controlling terminal and no display, so a repository test cannot exercise the interactive prompt path in any meaningful way. The regression was reproduced and verified manually instead, using the fake-launcher harness described under Reproducer (non-tty fallback path) and `script -qec` (pty path, where the prompt is shown on `/dev/tty`). The old code fails in both GUI and console modes; the new code passes. The existing `tests/test-oauth-pool-helper.sh` suite still passes (13/13).

## Notes

- The earlier `--no-open` PR #18846 was closed as completed via #18977, but that PR never carried the URL change. Automatic display detection plus always printing the URL covers the same use case without a flag.

- REST metadata parsing: three `jq` invocations → one, reused for the final attempt log.
- Plain `gh api ENDPOINT [--jq|-q EXPR]` GET fast path: skips loading write-policy, label-provisioning, and guard libraries. Any other shape (fields, `--input`, `-X/--method`, `--paginate`, `graphql`, `graphql/*`) keeps the full policy path.

## Acceptance revision (interactive maintainer decision)

The original ≤150 ms added-overhead target is not reachable without structural change. It is replaced with: **measured mechanical reduction on the plain-read path, plus profiling that attributes the remaining cost**. Reasoning:

Governed REST read (`repos/.../issues/N --jq .state`), phase timing on, three runs:

| Phase | ms |
| --- | --- |
| Bash startup, library loads, preflight (≈10 ms Perl clock per marker included) | ~185 (≈85 real) |
| Governor Python startup/imports | ~58 |
| `credential_identity` (`gh auth token` spawn) | ~60 |
| SQLite open + admission | ~6 |
| **Deliberate quota pacing** | **287–1170** |
| Native `gh` child | 388–601 |
| Metadata parse + telemetry append | ~65 |

Mechanical overhead is ≈270 ms. Wall time is dominated by deliberate pacing, because the shared REST-core pool runs at ~3,500–4,150 of 5,000/h. Credential lookup stays per call on purpose: the token is pinned only to the native child, never exported to long-lived parents. The larger throughput levers are fewer calls: #33068 (caller attribution) and #32638 (dispatch ceremony).

Wall time, timing off, zero-cost `rate_limit` read, 9 runs per variant, 2 rounds (medians, ms):

| Variant | Round 1 | Round 2 | Added vs native |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Native `gh` | 323 | 313 | — |
| Deployed shim (main) | 678 | 729 | 355–416 |
| This branch | 617 | 662 | 294–349 |

This is ≈60 ms (~15%) less mechanical overhead per plain read. For governed reads the saving is smaller than pacing variance, as expected.

## Worker evidence (retained)

The worker's earlier serial and concurrent measurements showed native 368–497 ms vs shim 764–7001 ms. The concurrent spread matched deliberate pacing (396–5921 ms), while SQLite admission itself took 4–64 ms.

title: GH#33068: perf(gh-api): attribute timeout-wrapped and session-origin REST calls
body:
Resolves #33068

## Root cause (sampled evidence)

I sampled live `gh` shim processes for 4 minutes on the maintainer runner and replayed the shim's own caller algorithm on each (script: process basenames only, no arguments):

- 169 distinct REST shim processes: 94 attributed from a parent script, **75 (44%) generic**.
- **All 75** had `timeout` as their immediate parent: `timeout < pulse-merge-routine.sh` 51, `timeout < pulse-wrapper.sh` 24.

`_shim_parent_framework_caller` only looked through shell/env launchers. `timeout 30 gh api …` is the framework's standard read pattern, so every timeout-wrapped call fell back to `gh_api_rest`. That also explains the `pulse-review-explicit-page` rows the issue flagged.

## Change (`.agents/scripts/gh-native-transport-lib.sh` only)

1. Walk past transparent process wrappers (`timeout`, `gtimeout`, `nice`, `nohup`, `stdbuf`, `caffeinate`), at most 3 levels, with one `ps -o ppid=,command=` per level. The command-line matching moved unchanged into `_shim_command_framework_caller`.
2. Session-role fallback: when no framework script is found, map the already-exported `AIDEVOPS_SESSION_ORIGIN` through a fixed allowlist (`worker`, `interactive`, `pulse`, `routine`, `conversation`) to `session-<role>`. Values are never copied verbatim; anything else keeps the subcommand label.
3. Precedence: `AIDEVOPS_GH_CALLER` (framework file) → parent framework script → session role → subcommand label.

No new session-start exports were needed: workers (`pulse-dispatch-worker-launch.sh`, `headless-runtime-run.sh`), the OpenCode plugin (interactive), and the launcher (conversation) already export `AIDEVOPS_SESSION_ORIGIN`. The caller value is logging-only; quota admission, pacing, and trust behaviour are unchanged. Step 4 of the brief (per-process parent-lookup cache) is not applicable, because each shim process resolves its caller once.

## Verification

Throwaway harness: a real process tree `framework-script → [wrapper] → shim-stand-in`, with `_SHIM_DIR` containing the framework script:

| Case | Old (deployed) | New |
| --- | --- | --- |
| direct | `fake-framework-caller.sh` | `fake-framework-caller.sh` |
| `timeout` | `gh_api_rest` | `fake-framework-caller.sh` |
| `nice timeout` | `gh_api_rest` | `fake-framework-caller.sh` |
| `$(timeout …)` | `gh_api_rest` | `fake-framework-caller.sh` |
| no framework parent, origin unset | — | `gh_api_rest` |
| no framework parent, origin=worker | — | `session-worker` |
| origin=`worker;rm` (injection) | — | `gh_api_rest` |
| framework parent + origin=worker | — | framework script wins |

- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/gh-native-transport-lib.sh`: clean
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-shim.sh`, `test-gh-api-instrument.sh`, `test-full-loop-worktree-gh-shim.sh`: pass, with `AIDEVOPS_SESSION_ORIGIN` both unset and `=interactive`

Post-deploy acceptance (≤10% generic over 6 h, plus a top-10 breakdown of formerly generic volume) will be posted on #33068 once this is released and has run for 6 h.

title: t18558: fix(prefetch): bound events-tickle skip by snapshot age (GH#33074)
body:
Resolves #33074

## Summary

The batch prefetch skipped an owner's refresh whenever the L1 events tickle returned 304. For organisations the tickle polls `/orgs/{org}/events`, which lists **public events only**. On a maintainer install with a private-repo org among its pulse owners, the ETag had not changed since 2026-08-19. The tickle reported "fresh" 48 times in a row, and that org's canonical issue and PR snapshots were 18–22 days stale.

Effects measured before this change:

- **API volume:** consumers fell back to a live `_prefetch_single_repo: full sweep` (non-conditional list reads) for that repo every cycle, instead of zero-cost conditional 304s.
- **Dispatch time (#32638):** the #33044 worker-draft negative cache needs a PR snapshot less than 900 s old, so it could never cache that repo's draft checkpoints. In 12 h, five of its issues were re-rejected 17–19 times each (6.6–10.9 min of dedup ceremony per issue). Repeat-rejected candidates (at least 5 attempts, never launched) accounted for 75% of all `dedup_check` time (160.9 min). Draft checkpoints on user-owned repos in the same window *were* cached.

## Change

- `pulse-events-tickle.sh`: `_PULSE_EVENTS_TICKLE_LAST_REASON` records why the call returned 0: `etag` (304) or `cooldown` (preflight, rate-limited response, or rate-limited org retry). The header documents the public-events limitation.
- `pulse-batch-prefetch-helper.sh`:
  - `_resolve_cache_snapshot` takes an optional max-age argument (default unchanged).
  - New `_owner_snapshots_recent` and `_events_tickle_skip_is_safe`.
  - `_cmd_refresh` honours cooldown skips as before. It honours ETag skips only while every owner snapshot is younger than `PULSE_EVENTS_TICKLE_MAX_CACHE_AGE` (default 900 s, the dispatch fingerprint bound). Otherwise it logs `events tickle fresh for owner=… but snapshots older than 900s — refreshing`, counts the owner as stale, and runs the normal conditional-REST refresh.
- `TODO.md`: t18558 entry.

A refresh that ignores the tickle costs at most two conditional GETs per repo. Those are free 304s when nothing changed.

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-batch-prefetch-conditional-rest.sh`: 31/31 pass, including three new cases:
  - an ETag 304 with stale snapshots refreshes (2 repo calls, snapshot restamped);
  - an ETag 304 with recent snapshots still skips (0 repo calls);
  - a cooldown still skips even with stale snapshots.
- **Negative control:** the same test run against `origin/main` versions of the two scripts fails the stale case with `repo_calls=0, prs_ts=2026-05-01T00:00:00Z`, which is the production symptom. The other two cases pass on both.
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-events-tickle.sh`: 32/32.
- `test-pulse-prefetch-canonical-snapshot.sh`, `test-pulse-cache-prime.sh`, `test-pulse-batch-refresh-timeout.sh`, `test-pulse-rate-limit-config-precedence.sh`: pass. `test-gh-api-instrument.sh`: 244/244; one earlier run hit a timing flake in an unrelated function-timeout case.
- `test-enrich-batch-prefetch.sh` fails the same two REST-fallback cases on unmodified `origin/main`, so it is pre-existing and not a regression.
- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/pulse-events-tickle.sh .agents/scripts/pulse-batch-prefetch-helper.sh`: clean.

## Post-deploy check

`pulse-batch-prefetch-helper.sh status` should show the private-org snapshots FRESH, and `pulse.log` should show `cross-cycle ownership block:worker_draft_checkpoint_blocked` for that repo's draft-checkpoint issues.

title: GH#33088: fix(session): What next asks only for what AI cannot do; options on own line
body:
## Summary

This PR follows up on PR #33083 with two changes to the `What next` block, both based on user feedback.

- **Ask only what the agent can't do.** Asks are limited to missing permission/authority, taste, inaccessible context, consequential ambiguity, unknown secrets, or human-only actions. ## Summary

This PR keeps the fixed-field `What next` block from #32628 and the numbered, low-typing asks from #33083/#33090, and fixes the drift shown in #33094.

title: t18561: fix(migrate-layout): skip verification for zero-row OpenCode DB consumers
body:
## Summary

`aidevops repos migrate-layout apply` failed with `OpenCode database verification failed: <isolated opencode.db>` after it had already moved the repository and updated the main OpenCode DB. The receipt was left partial.

## Root cause

The plan lists every isolated `opencode-interactive/*/opencode/opencode.db` as a database consumer. It keeps DBs with zero matching rows too, because they act as drift guards. Those DBs have an empty change set. `database_change_state()` reports an empty set as `"before"`, so `update_database()` ran an empty transaction. Its post-check then required `"after"` and raised. Any install with an unrelated isolated OpenCode DB hits this.

## Changes

- `.agents/scripts/repo_layout_migrate.py` `update_database()`: return early when `details["changes"]` is empty. `rollback_database()` already treats an empty set as `"before"` and returns, so rollback is unchanged.
- `tests/test-repo-layout-migrate.py`: the fixture now adds a second isolated DB that points at an unrelated path, giving a consumer with zero rows. The consumer-boundary resume test now also covers `consumer:database:2`.

## Verification

- Before the fix, the updated fixture reproduced the exact field error: 12 of 13 tests failed with `OpenCode database verification failed: .../isolated/worker-2/opencode/opencode.db`.
- After the fix, `python3 -W ignore::ResourceWarning tests/test-repo-layout-migrate.py` passed all 13 tests.

Resolves #33108

title: GH#33026: fix: stop pulse retrying issues whose reused worktree has an unchanged live owner
body:
## Summary

Root cause: a live registry owner refusing the reused-worktree claim was collapsed into worktree_precreation_failed, an infrastructure reason deliberately excluded from per-issue backoff, so the same issue was re-selected, claimed, canaried and refused every cycle. Now: (1) _dlw_precreate_worktree identifies an identity-verified live owner (PID + process-start generation, PID reuse excluded) after the atomic claim is rejected and reports a distinct worktree_live_owner_refused pre-runtime reason with one structured WORKTREE_LIVE_OWNER_REFUSED log line; SQLite/worktree-helper faults keep the generic reason and counter. (2) The existing dispatch negative cache records a per-issue hold keyed on owner PID + start token + worktree; the prefilter skips the candidate before claim/canary only while that exact owner generation is alive and still owns the worktree (owner exit, PID reuse or handover invalidates immediately; bounded by the existing <=30 min TTL; missing helpers fail open). It is keyed on owner identity rather than updatedAt because the refused attempt's own claim comment bumps updatedAt. (3) One diagnostic line when the held issue is OPEN with solved:worker; never auto-closes. The reason is classified launch-preflight so runners are not penalised. Owner rows are read only, never removed, reset or taken over. permission_required and metadata-read failures are untouched.

## Files Changed

.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib.sh, .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-worker-launch.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-precreation-failure-skip.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-stale-pr-continuation.sh, .agents/scripts/worker-lifecycle-common.sh

title: GH#33130: Prevent What next from hiding uncommitted work
body:
## Summary

- require a live Git-status check in every repository/worktree touched by an interactive session
- classify session-owned modified, staged, and untracked files as uncaptured until committed

The capture check covered deferred objectives and durable notes, but did not

title: GH#33025: fix: project trusted approvals into clean-room briefs and let collaborator runners open terminal-blocker circuits
body:
## Summary

Two root causes from the approved review. (1) Clean-room dispatch (pulse-dispatch-worker-prompt.sh) dropped comment-borne authority, so workers saw approval-pending bodies after a maintainer signed approval or posted terminal-blocker-circuit:retry. The dispatcher now projects metadata only (comment id, author, timestamp) for the newest OWNER/MEMBER signed-approval marker line and standalone retry directive into a Trusted authority block; comment text is never copied, quoted/prose look-alikes and non-OWNER/MEMBER authors are ignored and counted, and every clean-room launch logs approval/retry/ignored_untrusted. (2) terminal-blocker-circuit.sh accepted hold evidence only from OWNER/MEMBER, so a runner whose account is a bare COLLABORATOR (e.g. a bot on a personal private repo) never opened a circuit and redispatched identical blockers forever. Hold evidence (observations, circuits, blocked releases) now also accepts COLLABORATOR comments authored by this runner's own validated login (TERMINAL_BLOCKER_SELF_LOGIN, wired from dispatch-dedup-helper.sh, headless-runtime-failure.sh and terminal-blocker-recovery-helper.sh). Other collaborators stay ignored; only OWNER/MEMBER retry directives clear holds. Dropped hold-shaped evidence emits one TERMINAL_BLOCKER_EVIDENCE_IGNORED diagnostic.



## Files Changed

## Summary

Implementation for issue #32977: a Pulse refill batch no longer launches two workers whose declared file footprints overlap.

Before this change, each candidate ran its own dispatch subshell with a cold footprint cache. A worker only became visible to the overlap check once its status labels landed on GitHub, so overlapping candidates in one refill batch could both pass `_footprint_check_overlap`.

## Changes

- `.agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-footprint.sh`
  - Adds a per-repo reservation store (`~/.aidevops/cache/footprint-reservations`, 0700). Filenames use a hashed repo key, so private repo names never appear on disk. A per-repo `mkdir` lock breaks stale holders.
  - `_footprint_check_overlap` reads live labels outside the lock, then under the lock merges active reservations and checks overlap. If there is no overlap, it atomically writes this candidate's reservation (temp file, then `mv`). If the lock stays busy, it defers the candidate to the next cycle.
  - `status:queued` now counts as in-flight, both for live footprints and for the durable-defer blocker lifecycle.
  - Reservations end in one of three ways:
    - Released on a failed launch (`footprint_release_reservation`, scoped to the current attempt's epoch).
    - Stamped `superseded_at` once the issue's lifecycle labels are visible, then removed after a 120s grace period. The grace keeps a concurrent caller with a stale live read from missing it.
    - Expired after a 900s TTL.
  - Shared release/version files (`VERSION`, `CHANGELOG.md`, …) are low-information and do not block on their own. Any shared implementation file still blocks.
  - Bare list items in a canonical `## Files Scope` / `### Files Scope` section now count as a declared footprint. Paths elsewhere stay context-only.
  - Moves the parallel active-label fetch into `_footprint_fetch_active_issues`.
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib.sh`: `_dispatch_process_candidate` releases this attempt's reservation when dispatch fails or times out, and when launch validation fails.
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-footprint-overlap.sh`: batch-reservation cases required by the issue acceptance criteria.

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Medium (dispatch gating)
- **Live read-only check** against `marcusquinn/aidevops` with temp reservation/defer stores and no GitHub writes:
  - The active-label fetch returned 6 live issues.
  - Candidate #33097 (5 declared paths) passed and was reserved (`event=reserved`).
  - A second same-batch candidate with the same footprint got `FOOTPRINT_OVERLAP (issue=#33097 files=…)` via the reservation.
  - `footprint_release_reservation` cleared it (`event=released`, 0 files left).
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-footprint-overlap.sh`: 29 run, 0 failed.
- ShellCheck clean on all three files. `complexity-regression-helper.sh check`: no new violations.
- Related suites show no regressions. The failures that appear occur identically on clean `main` at `12d407826f`:
  - `test-dispatch-max-parallel.sh`: 1 failure (REST reserve-adjacent zone).
  - `test-pulse-current-state-guardrails.sh`: 2 failures.
  - `test-pulse-wrapper-silent-dispatch.sh`: 4 failures.
  - These suites pass: `test-pulse-dispatch-candidate-snapshot`, `test-pulse-dispatch-core-external-author-gate`, `test-pulse-dispatch-idle-debt-borrowing`, `test-pulse-dep-graph-bash32-nul-crash`, `test-pulse-diagnose-helper`, `test-dispatch-candidate-failure-reasons`.

## Limits

Reservations are local to one runner. Cross-runner overlap still relies on GitHub status labels, as before.

Resolves #32977

title: GH#33132: fix: surface one approval-ready attention record when a blocked worker leaves a draft checkpoint
body:
## Summary

Resolves #33132

A worker that releases as `blocked` after opening a draft PR leaves the objective held by `WORKER_DRAFT_CHECKPOINT`. That hold is intentional: a blocked checkpoint must never auto-continue without the revision-bound approval from GH#31265 / PR #31269. But until now nothing told the brief owner that an approval (or a draft close) was the required next step, so the objective stalled silently.

This PR keeps the approval-bound invariant and adds no continuation path. When Pulse hits the draft checkpoint block, it now asks the continuation helper to post **one** deduplicated, actionable attention record.

## Changes

- `.agents/scripts/pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh`: new `blocked-attention <repo> <issue> <pr>` command.
  - Posts only when the draft is open, the newest trusted `CLAIM_RELEASED` is the PR author's `reason=blocked` release, and no later coordination event (claim, lease, dispatch, release, interactive claim) shows another owner.
  - Deduplicates by PR head and release ID via a hidden marker.
  - Names the release comment ID and the original ready-lease attempt, so the `approval-template` command in the body is ready to run. It lists both exits: correct the brief and approve, or close the draft to restart ordinary dispatch.
  - No body line starts with a coordination or approval prefix, so `pr_checkpoint_events` release/successor validation for a later approval is unaffected. It grants nothing, changes no labels or assignees, and never dispatches.
  - The usage text now lists every subcommand.
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-dedup-layers.sh`: layer 4 calls the helper on a best-effort basis before returning the existing `WORKER_DRAFT_CHECKPOINT` block (rc 2 is unchanged).
- `.agents/reference/checkpoint-revision-recovery.md`: documents the attention record.

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh`: 36/36 pass. New cases: blocked release plus draft posts one record; the record forges no events; later cycles dedup it; newer ownership suppresses it; a non-blocked checkpoint is unaffected; a ready PR is not treated as a draft checkpoint.
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-stale-pr-continuation.sh`: 26/26 pass with GNU `date`, as on Linux CI. New case: the layer-4 draft checkpoint requests blocked attention and still blocks. On macOS, BSD `date -d` fails one existing case, before and after this PR.
- `test-terminal-blocker-circuit.sh` (20/20), `test-headless-runtime-completion-tests.sh`, `test-headless-runtime-checkpoint-tests.sh`: pass.
- `shellcheck` is clean on all changed scripts; `markdownlint-cli2` is clean on the changed doc.

Unrelated, and present before this PR: `test-pulse-wrapper-terminal-blockers.sh` fails locally on "gh --slurp blocker includes prerequisite guidance". It covers `pulse-dispatch-core.sh`, which this PR does not touch.

title: GH#33172: scope-guard compares against origin/main, not stale local main

## Summary

title: GH#33243: fix(dispatch): let workers own Files Scope discovery instead of holding trusted unscoped briefs
body:
## Summary

Root cause of the recent status:blocked growth: since GH#32531 the pre-claim gate parks any auto-dispatch brief without a canonical Files Scope as status:blocked (missing_files_scope, owner=brief-author). The authors are AI sessions that have already ended, so nobody returns; 10 of 14 open blocked issues on 2026-09-30 had this marker. This PR makes the pulse dispatch trusted-author unscoped briefs instead, and the worker's first step is scope discovery: it records a canonical ### Files Scope on the issue before editing (new worker-discipline section 'Missing Files Scope', worker contract and first-pass prompt updated). Existing trusted brief holds are released automatically when the hold is still the newest blocker. Untrusted authors stay blocked, deterministic normalization still runs first, creation-time gates stay (the author has the most context) with corrected messages, and AIDEVOPS_BRIEF_SCOPE_WORKER_DISCOVERY=0 restores the old hold.

title: GH#33256: fix(pulse): async housekeeping survives launchd process-group teardown
body:
## Summary

Async post-dispatch housekeeping was launched as a disowned subshell inside the pulse wrapper's process group. The launchd pulse job has no AbandonProcessGroup, so launchd kills the group when pulse-wrapper.sh exits. pulse.log shows 50 launches, 11 completions and 38 stale-lock reclaims; recent runs die mid-stage exactly at the next 'pulse-wrapper invoked' line. Everything after the kill point was skipped, including the GH#33246 blocker-refresh catch-up and preflight_ownership_reconcile, and dep-graph-cache.json was last written 2026-09-29T07:16. Fix: _pulse_start_post_dispatch_housekeeping turns on bash job control (set -m) only around the background launch, so the subshell gets its own process group, then restores the caller's monitor mode. The subshell turns job control off again, so stages run as before. Stage timeouts kill by parent tree (pgrep -P), so they are unaffected; the existing lock and per-stage timeouts still bound a hung run. Not addressed: Linux systemd kills by cgroup, and that path is unverified. The merge-first kick in pulse-dispatch-preflight-lib.sh uses nohup only and may share the problem, but there is no evidence yet.



## Files Changed

.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-post-dispatch-housekeeping.sh

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Medium
- **Verification:** self-assessed — Regression: the async test now asserts that the child PGID differs from the launcher's and that monitor mode is restored. Negative control with the engine change stashed: FAIL 'child pgid=83130 shares launcher pgid=83130'; with the fix: 4/4 PASS. test-pulse-dispatch-engine-stage-wiring.sh: 61/61. ShellCheck clean. Probe: a non-TTY /opt/homebrew/bin/bash gives the child a distinct PGID with no warnings. Live verification (housekeeping 'complete' lines, refreshed dep-graph cache) follows the deploy.

title: chore(deps): bump urllib3 from 2.7.0 to 2.8.0 in the pip group across 1 directory
body:
Bumps the pip group with 1 update in the / directory: [urllib3](https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3). Updates `urllib3` from 2.7.0 to 2.8.0
Release notes

Sourced from urllib3's releases.

2.8.0

🚀 urllib3 is fundraising for HTTP/2 support

urllib3 is raising ~$40,000 USD to release HTTP/2 support and ensure long-term sustainable maintenance of the project. If your company or organization uses Python and would benefit from HTTP/2 support in Requests, pip, cloud SDKs, and thousands of other projects please consider contributing financially to ensure HTTP/2 support is developed sustainably and maintained for the long-haul.

Thank you for your support.

Security

Fixed the following security issues:

  • The TLS configuration for HTTPS proxies could be ignored or overridden. (High severity, GHSA-8988-9cw3-xx77)
  • HTTPResponse.stream() and read_chunked() could buffer a chunk-size line of unbounded length in memory. (High severity, GHSA-vxq7-64xx-v4gw)
  • Chunked Deflate streaming could enter an infinite loop. (Medium severity, GHSA-gh4c-6fx4-qh6g)

[!IMPORTANT] urllib3 2.8.0 fixes HTTPS proxy TLS configuration being ignored or overridden by destination settings. Configurations relying on that behavior may require changes.

Configure proxy CA certificates and client certificates in proxy_ssl_context, and proxy identity checks with proxy_assert_hostname or proxy_assert_fingerprint. Destination client certificates and identity overrides no longer apply to HTTPS forwarding proxy connections.

[!NOTE] CVE IDs had not yet been assigned to these advisories at the time of release due to a backlog at GitHub's CNA.

Deprecations & Removals

  • Deprecated using an empty collection as the Retry option allowed_methods to retry any verb. (#5044)

Features

  • Added Url.auth_decoded and Url.auth_decoded_joined convenience properties to the result of parse_url(). (#4945)
  • Added basic_auth_encoding and proxy_basic_auth_encoding parameters to urllib3.util.make_headers(). (#5092)

Bugfixes

  • Fixed response header handling to replace obsolete folded header lines (obs-fold) with spaces in accordance with RFC 9112, preventing raw CRLF sequences from appearing in header values such as Set-Cookie. (#1362)

  • Fixed usage of proxy_ssl_context with ProxyManager when use_forwarding_for_https=True. Passing ssl_context instead of proxy_ssl_context for HTTPS proxies in this configuration now emits a FutureWarning and will raise an error in v3.0. (#2577)

  • Changed behavior of the default ConnectionPool.pool initialization. LifoQueue is now resolved from the queue module after the ConnectionPool is instantiated instead of using the default cached QueueCls class property. This is done because sometimes the queue.LifoQueue is monkey-patched late in the program, such as by gevent. (#3289)

  • Raised UnrewindableBodyError instead of ValueError when retrying a request whose body had tell() but not seek(). (#3779)

  • Decoded percent-encoded SOCKS proxy credentials before authenticating with the proxy server. (#3785)

  • Fixed HTTPResponse.drain_conn() to discard unread response data in 64 KiB chunks (same as the default amt when doing HTTPResponse.stream(...)). (#5019)

  • Fixed is_ipaddress() to detect non-standard IPv4 forms accepted by socket.connect, such as hex (0x7f000001), octal (0177.0.0.1), and decimal integers (2130706433), ensuring SSL certificate verification uses the correct mode for these addresses. (#5029)

  • Fixed HTTPConnectionPool.urlopen raising a misleading FullPoolError instead of ValueError when called with an invalid timeout argument on a pool created with block=True. (#5059)

  • Fixed port-zero handling to preserve explicit :0 values instead of substituting the default ports 80 or 443 in URL parsing, pool selection, proxy configuration, connection_from_url(), and HTTP/2 request authority. (#5071, #5101)

  • Fixed a bug where PoolManager passed the assert_hostname and assert_fingerprint parameters to HTTP connection pools. (#5077)

  • Fixed HTTPConnectionPool.urlopen() and HTTP proxy forwarding to strip URL fragments from absolute request targets before sending requests. (#5079)

  • Added safeguards to the proxy tunneling code to prevent potential security issues when handling invalid characters in the proxy host and HTTP headers. This change affects users of Python 3.10, Python 3.11, and Python 3.12 when the standard library does not contain the fix; those on newer Python versions should upgrade to 3.13.14+ or 3.14.5+ to get the same security fixes. (#5091)

  • Fixed HTTPSConnection.connect() overriding ProxyConfig.ssl_context's certificate policy and proxy identity checks with the target connection's TLS settings when forwarding through an HTTPS proxy.

    HTTPSConnection no longer applies target SNI, assertions, or client credentials to forwarding proxy handshakes and continues to use its ssl_context as a fallback when an HTTPS proxy forwards an HTTP target. (#5093)

  • Fixed URL parsing to more strictly enforce RFC 3986 host syntax, rejecting invalid host input such as raw spaces and control characters, malformed percent-encodings, and percent-encoded control characters in HTTP(S) hosts and IPv6 zone identifiers, including proxy CONNECT tunnel targets. Host normalization now also follows RFC 3986 normalization rules for percent-encoded octets by decoding percent-encoded unreserved characters and uppercasing the hexadecimal digits of retained percent-encoded octets. (#5095)

... (truncated)

Changelog

Sourced from urllib3's changelog.

Security

body:
Bumps the pip group with 1 update in the / directory: [urllib3](https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3). Updates `urllib3` from 2.7.0 to 2.8.0
Release notes

Sourced from urllib3's releases.

2.8.0

🚀 urllib3 is fundraising for HTTP/2 support

urllib3 is raising ~$40,000 USD to release HTTP/2 support and ensure long-term sustainable maintenance of the project. If your company or organization uses Python and would benefit from HTTP/2 support in Requests, pip, cloud SDKs, and thousands of other projects please consider contributing financially to ensure HTTP/2 support is developed sustainably and maintained for the long-haul.

Thank you for your support.

Security

Fixed the following security issues:

  • The TLS configuration for HTTPS proxies could be ignored or overridden. (High severity, GHSA-8988-9cw3-xx77)
  • HTTPResponse.stream() and read_chunked() could buffer a chunk-size line of unbounded length in memory. (High severity, GHSA-vxq7-64xx-v4gw)
  • Chunked Deflate streaming could enter an infinite loop. (Medium severity, GHSA-gh4c-6fx4-qh6g)

[!IMPORTANT] urllib3 2.8.0 fixes HTTPS proxy TLS configuration being ignored or overridden by destination settings. Configurations relying on that behavior may require changes.

Configure proxy CA certificates and client certificates in proxy_ssl_context, and proxy identity checks with proxy_assert_hostname or proxy_assert_fingerprint. Destination client certificates and identity overrides no longer apply to HTTPS forwarding proxy connections.

[!NOTE] CVE IDs had not yet been assigned to these advisories at the time of release due to a backlog at GitHub's CNA.

Deprecations & Removals

  • Deprecated using an empty collection as the Retry option allowed_methods to retry any verb. (#5044)

Features

  • Added Url.auth_decoded and Url.auth_decoded_joined convenience properties to the result of parse_url(). (#4945)
  • Added basic_auth_encoding and proxy_basic_auth_encoding parameters to urllib3.util.make_headers(). (#5092)

Bugfixes

  • Fixed response header handling to replace obsolete folded header lines (obs-fold) with spaces in accordance with RFC 9112, preventing raw CRLF sequences from appearing in header values such as Set-Cookie. (#1362)

  • Fixed usage of proxy_ssl_context with ProxyManager when use_forwarding_for_https=True. Passing ssl_context instead of proxy_ssl_context for HTTPS proxies in this configuration now emits a FutureWarning and will raise an error in v3.0. (#2577)

  • Changed behavior of the default ConnectionPool.pool initialization. LifoQueue is now resolved from the queue module after the ConnectionPool is instantiated instead of using the default cached QueueCls class property. This is done because sometimes the queue.LifoQueue is monkey-patched late in the program, such as by gevent. (#3289)

  • Raised UnrewindableBodyError instead of ValueError when retrying a request whose body had tell() but not seek(). (#3779)

  • Decoded percent-encoded SOCKS proxy credentials before authenticating with the proxy server. (#3785)

  • Fixed HTTPResponse.drain_conn() to discard unread response data in 64 KiB chunks (same as the default amt when doing HTTPResponse.stream(...)). (#5019)

  • Fixed is_ipaddress() to detect non-standard IPv4 forms accepted by socket.connect, such as hex (0x7f000001), octal (0177.0.0.1), and decimal integers (2130706433), ensuring SSL certificate verification uses the correct mode for these addresses. (#5029)

  • Fixed HTTPConnectionPool.urlopen raising a misleading FullPoolError instead of ValueError when called with an invalid timeout argument on a pool created with block=True. (#5059)

  • Fixed port-zero handling to preserve explicit :0 values instead of substituting the default ports 80 or 443 in URL parsing, pool selection, proxy configuration, connection_from_url(), and HTTP/2 request authority. (#5071, #5101)

  • Fixed a bug where PoolManager passed the assert_hostname and assert_fingerprint parameters to HTTP connection pools. (#5077)

  • Fixed HTTPConnectionPool.urlopen() and HTTP proxy forwarding to strip URL fragments from absolute request targets before sending requests. (#5079)

  • Added safeguards to the proxy tunneling code to prevent potential security issues when handling invalid characters in the proxy host and HTTP headers. This change affects users of Python 3.10, Python 3.11, and Python 3.12 when the standard library does not contain the fix; those on newer Python versions should upgrade to 3.13.14+ or 3.14.5+ to get the same security fixes. (#5091)

  • Fixed HTTPSConnection.connect() overriding ProxyConfig.ssl_context's certificate policy and proxy identity checks with the target connection's TLS settings when forwarding through an HTTPS proxy.

    HTTPSConnection no longer applies target SNI, assertions, or client credentials to forwarding proxy handshakes and continues to use its ssl_context as a fallback when an HTTPS proxy forwards an HTTP target. (#5093)

  • Fixed URL parsing to more strictly enforce RFC 3986 host syntax, rejecting invalid host input such as raw spaces and control characters, malformed percent-encodings, and percent-encoded control characters in HTTP(S) hosts and IPv6 zone identifiers, including proxy CONNECT tunnel targets. Host normalization now also follows RFC 3986 normalization rules for percent-encoded octets by decoding percent-encoded unreserved characters and uppercasing the hexadecimal digits of retained percent-encoded octets. (#5095)

Updates `urllib3` from 2.7.0 to 2.8.0
Release notes

Sourced from urllib3's releases.

2.8.0

🚀 urllib3 is fundraising for HTTP/2 support

urllib3 is raising ~$40,000 USD to release HTTP/2 support and ensure long-term sustainable maintenance of the project. If your company or organization uses Python and would benefit from HTTP/2 support in Requests, pip, cloud SDKs, and thousands of other projects please consider contributing financially to ensure HTTP/2 support is developed sustainably and maintained for the long-haul.

Thank you for your support.

Security

Fixed the following security issues:

  • The TLS configuration for HTTPS proxies could be ignored or overridden. (High severity, GHSA-8988-9cw3-xx77)
  • HTTPResponse.stream() and read_chunked() could buffer a chunk-size line of unbounded length in memory. (High severity, GHSA-vxq7-64xx-v4gw)
  • Chunked Deflate streaming could enter an infinite loop. (Medium severity, GHSA-gh4c-6fx4-qh6g)

[!IMPORTANT] urllib3 2.8.0 fixes HTTPS proxy TLS configuration being ignored or overridden by destination settings. Configurations relying on that behavior may require changes.

Configure proxy CA certificates and client certificates in proxy_ssl_context, and proxy identity checks with proxy_assert_hostname or proxy_assert_fingerprint. Destination client certificates and identity overrides no longer apply to HTTPS forwarding proxy connections.

[!NOTE] CVE IDs had not yet been assigned to these advisories at the time of release due to a backlog at GitHub's CNA.

Deprecations & Removals

  • Deprecated using an empty collection as the Retry option allowed_methods to retry any verb. (#5044)

Features

  • Added Url.auth_decoded and Url.auth_decoded_joined convenience properties to the result of parse_url(). (#4945)
  • Added basic_auth_encoding and proxy_basic_auth_encoding parameters to urllib3.util.make_headers(). (#5092)

Bugfixes

  • Fixed response header handling to replace obsolete folded header lines (obs-fold) with spaces in accordance with RFC 9112, preventing raw CRLF sequences from appearing in header values such as Set-Cookie. (#1362)

  • Fixed usage of proxy_ssl_context with ProxyManager when use_forwarding_for_https=True. Passing ssl_context instead of proxy_ssl_context for HTTPS proxies in this configuration now emits a FutureWarning and will raise an error in v3.0. (#2577)

  • Changed behavior of the default ConnectionPool.pool initialization. LifoQueue is now resolved from the queue module after the ConnectionPool is instantiated instead of using the default cached QueueCls class property. This is done because sometimes the queue.LifoQueue is monkey-patched late in the program, such as by gevent. (#3289)

  • Raised UnrewindableBodyError instead of ValueError when retrying a request whose body had tell() but not seek(). (#3779)

  • Decoded percent-encoded SOCKS proxy credentials before authenticating with the proxy server. (#3785)

  • Fixed HTTPResponse.drain_conn() to discard unread response data in 64 KiB chunks (same as the default amt when doing HTTPResponse.stream(...)). (#5019)

  • Fixed is_ipaddress() to detect non-standard IPv4 forms accepted by socket.connect, such as hex (0x7f000001), octal (0177.0.0.1), and decimal integers (2130706433), ensuring SSL certificate verification uses the correct mode for these addresses. (#5029)

  • Fixed HTTPConnectionPool.urlopen raising a misleading FullPoolError instead of ValueError when called with an invalid timeout argument on a pool created with block=True. (#5059)

  • Fixed port-zero handling to preserve explicit :0 values instead of substituting the default ports 80 or 443 in URL parsing, pool selection, proxy configuration, connection_from_url(), and HTTP/2 request authority. (#5071, #5101)

  • Fixed a bug where PoolManager passed the assert_hostname and assert_fingerprint parameters to HTTP connection pools. (#5077)

  • Fixed HTTPConnectionPool.urlopen() and HTTP proxy forwarding to strip URL fragments from absolute request targets before sending requests. (#5079)

  • Added safeguards to the proxy tunneling code to prevent potential security issues when handling invalid characters in the proxy host and HTTP headers. This change affects users of Python 3.10, Python 3.11, and Python 3.12 when the standard library does not contain the fix; those on newer Python versions should upgrade to 3.13.14+ or 3.14.5+ to get the same security fixes. (#5091)

  • Fixed HTTPSConnection.connect() overriding ProxyConfig.ssl_context's certificate policy and proxy identity checks with the target connection's TLS settings when forwarding through an HTTPS proxy.

    HTTPSConnection no longer applies target SNI, assertions, or client credentials to forwarding proxy handshakes and continues to use its ssl_context as a fallback when an HTTPS proxy forwards an HTTP target. (#5093)

  • Fixed URL parsing to more strictly enforce RFC 3986 host syntax, rejecting invalid host input such as raw spaces and control characters, malformed percent-encodings, and percent-encoded control characters in HTTP(S) hosts and IPv6 zone identifiers, including proxy CONNECT tunnel targets. Host normalization now also follows RFC 3986 normalization rules for percent-encoded octets by decoding percent-encoded unreserved characters and uppercasing the hexadecimal digits of retained percent-encoded octets. (#5095)

Gate 3 of _consolidation_skip_if_resolved now collects merged closing PRs and filters them through _ddpr_first_merge_after_reopen (GH#33071, lazily sourced from dispatch-dedup-pr.sh): a PR merged before the issue's latest reopen no longer counts as resolved; lookup errors fail open. _dispatch_issue_consolidation records _CONSOLIDATION_DISPATCH_OUTCOME=preflight_skipped, and _dispatch_dedup_scope_gates continues to the remaining gates instead of deferring forever when no consolidation child will exist. title: feat(wordpress): plugin release build, WordPress.org preflight and Plugin Check helper + submission guide (#33301)
body:
## Summary

Adds a reusable WordPress plugin release and WordPress.org preflight capability for any plugin repository, per #33301.

- `NEW: .agents/scripts/wp-plugin-release-helper.sh` — `build`, `preflight`, and `plugin-check` subcommands. Never tags, pushes, publishes, uploads, or commits.
- `NEW: .agents/tools/wordpress/wp-plugin-release.md` — two release channels (GitHub/Git Updater and WordPress.org), per-channel exclusions, the preflight checklist, and the WordPress.org submission checklist with official Plugin Handbook sources.
- `EDIT: .agents/tools/wordpress/wp-dev.md` — points to the new doc/helper.
- `EDIT: .agents/subagent-index.toon` — adds `wp-plugin-release` to the `tools/wordpress/` list.

## Verification

Ran against a scratch plugin fixture (not committed to this repo):

- `build`: produces `<slug>-X.Y.Z.zip` and `wordpress-org-<slug>-X.Y.Z.zip`, each with one `<slug>/` top folder; repeated builds give identical `SHA256SUMS`.
- `preflight --offline`: exits 0 on the clean fixture; exits 1 with three `ERROR`s (non-release `Version:`, `Update URI` header, `Stable tag` mismatch) on a deliberately broken fixture committed to a throwaway local branch, plus the new Text Domain / License / `*_VERSION` constant / readme-naming / tag-exists checks against the clean fixture.
- `plugin-check`: ran the official Plugin Check plugin against both zips in a disposable Docker WordPress + MariaDB stack; correctly surfaced an `ERROR`-level `outdated_tested_upto_header` finding (exit 1), and left no containers, volumes, or networks behind afterward (`docker ps -a`/`network ls`/`volume ls` filtered on the run prefix were empty both before and after).
- `shellcheck` and `shfmt`: clean.
- `.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh --changed`: whitespace, string-literal, ShellCheck, Secretlint, and Markdown checks all pass (the file-size ratchet warning is pre-existing and unrelated to this change).
- Confirmed no `git tag`, `git push`, `gh release`, or `svn ci|commit` in the helper (only in `wp-plugin-release.md` documentation prose).

### Fix found during verification

The initial `plugin-check` implementation left Docker containers/volumes/networks running when Plugin Check reported an `ERROR` finding: with `set -euo pipefail`, a bare failing `[[ ... ]]` as the final statement of `wprh_cmd_plugin_check` triggered immediate script termination, skipping the function's `RETURN` cleanup trap. Fixed by capturing the test result into a local variable before `return`, so cleanup always runs. Re-verified with a real Docker run that the fix resolves the leak.

Resolves #33301

title: GH#33307: fix(pulse): reserve dispatch budget and attribute merge-pass time
body:
## Summary

Resolves #33307

Batch dispatch was starved for 45+ minutes: the pre-dispatch merge pass consumed the cycle budget (`total_s=356` with only ~37s attributed), so `dispatch_max` ran with negative remaining budget (`-201s`, `-458s`, `-883s`) and logged `implementation_dispatched=0`. Each exhausted pass still enumerated every candidate and consumed the refill trigger, pushing the cycle further past its budget.

## Changes

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh`
  - Merge-only stages (`deterministic_merge_pass`, `dirty_pr_sweep`) now run with `AIDEVOPS_PULSE_CYCLE_FINALISE_RESERVE_S` raised by one per-candidate floor. The existing graceful merge deadline (`pulse-merge-pass.sh`) and stage clamp (`pulse-watchdog.sh`) both honour it, so long backlogs pause at the PR cursor and resume next cycle.
  - New admission gate `_pulse_cycle_budget_admits_dispatch` skips `dispatch_max` and the cycle-final refill drain **before** candidate enumeration when remaining budget < floor. The refill trigger is retained for a fresh-budget worker-exit refill or next cycle. Missing/invalid cycle clock fails open.
  - Opt-out: `AIDEVOPS_PULSE_DISPATCH_BUDGET_RESERVE=0`. `DISPATCH_PER_CANDIDATE_TIMEOUT_FLOOR` (600s) is unchanged; the per-candidate early-stop remains for genuinely overrun cycles.
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-process.sh`, `pulse-merge-pass.sh`, `pulse-merge-timing.sh`
  - Per-repo `deterministic_merge_pass timing:` line adds `enrichment_s`, `pr_s` (whole per-PR unit), `other_s` (remaining overhead) and `slowest_pr=#N:Ss`, making `total_s` explainable. Existing fields are unchanged (appended only).
  - Extracted cache setup/cleanup and timed-enrichment helpers to keep `_merge_ready_prs_for_repo` under the 100-line function gate.

## Verification

- `shellcheck` on all four scripts: clean.
- Existing tests pass: `test-pulse-merge-timing-summary`, `test-pulse-merge-pr-cursor-resume` (38), `test-pulse-wrapper-characterization` (54), `test-pulse-dispatch-engine-stage-wiring` (61), `test-pulse-event-refill` (29), `test-pulse-merge-routine-timeout` (9), `test-pulse-graphql-budget-priority`.
- `test-pulse-merge-routine-standalone` 25/25 when the session's inherited `AIDEVOPS_GH_PR_VIEW_CACHE_DIR` is unset (test 6d fails identically on `origin/main` under that env; environment leak, not this change).
- `complexity-regression-helper.sh check` for function-complexity, nesting-depth, file-size, bash32-compat: no new violations.
- Ad-hoc check: admission gate admits at 710s remaining, skips at 510s with the logged reason, fails open without `PULSE_START_EPOCH`; per-PR accumulator and `slowest_pr` computed correctly.

Post-deploy log check: `rg -n "per-candidate floor|implementation_dispatched=|skipped before candidate enumeration|enrichment_s=" ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log`

title: GH#33150: re-sync Remotion and Cloudflare platform skills from upstream
body:
Resolves #33150

## Summary

Re-sync Remotion and the official Cloudflare skills through a repeatable, registry-owned importer. Preserve the original PR commits and integrate the default branch with a merge; the existing PR branch is advanced without rewriting history.

- Remotion: 70 generated files under `.agents/tools/video/remotion/`, with `remotion.md` as the router. Preserve the local integration preamble, HeyGen/Three.js references and Higgsfield rendering code. Repair all active inbound links to the moved router.
- Cloudflare: 160 generated files from `cloudflare/skills`, including the current product-selection decision table, gotchas, and full references for Containers, Agents SDK, AI Search, Sandbox, RealtimeKit, Workflows and Basin. Generic pattern sets and Pulumi/Terraform/Turnstile trees remain excluded.
- Machine-readable policy: `.agents/configs/skill-sources.json`, each skill's `import_policy` v1 (`rules`, `exclude`, `resource_path`, `index_source`, `preserve_before`, and Remotion `link_aliases`). Replace the unsupported `skill-md-nested-multi` label with implemented `skill-md-curated` handling.
- `.agents/scripts/add-skill-helper-curated.sh` consumes those policies, stages validated mappings, transposes links, normalizes Markdown presentation, preserves unknown custom files and retains provenance/policy fields on registration. Security scanning happens before installed-file mutation.
- `.agents/scripts/add-skill-helper-import.sh` loads and routes curated conversion; the small early dispatch in `add-skill-helper-commands.sh` prevents openskills or guessed placement from bypassing the policy. `skill-update-core-lib.sh` propagates import/scanner failure. Explicit and automatic named updates use the same add path.
- Setup migration removes only exact historical leaves, guards files still present in the current source, and avoids recursive deletion of user-owned resource directories.

## Root cause

The previous registry described trims only in prose and recorded a format the importer did not implement. Updates rediscovered placement and the first nested skill, so they could recreate retired paths or re-import excluded documents. Policy selection now precedes format/path inference and remains in the registry after every sync.

## Verification

- Actual upstream imports through `skill-update-helper.sh update remotion` and `update cloudflare-platform-skill`, with security scans enabled. Recorded upstream commits: Remotion `0b5db9daae40f42c73544d1cc0a8c733bd530eaa`; Cloudflare `41e0d19858946d18af9ee2c2feebbe2e11d829ff`.
- Scoped `skill-update-helper.sh check --quiet --json` against an isolated registry containing both skills: 2 up to date, 0 updates, 0 failed lookups.
- `bash tests/test-skill-url-update-flow.sh`: 36 assertions pass. Each real registry policy is imported twice through the normal update command with deterministic upstream fixtures; generated file/hash manifests are byte-identical. Excludes and canonical targets remain stable, custom files survive, and a rejected HIGH scanner fixture fails the update without changing registration.

title: fix: skip tap-qualified Homebrew formulas on hosts without brew
body:
Resolves #33337

## Summary

On Linux hosts with `apt-get` but without Homebrew, `aidevops update` could fail every run with:

```
sudo apt-get install --only-upgrade -y steveyegge/beads/bd
E: Unable to locate package steveyegge/beads
Tool maintenance failed: 1 action(s) did not complete or verify.
```

## Root cause

`_tool_latest_version` (`.agents/scripts/tool-version-check.sh`) resolved the latest version for `brew` entries via `get_apt_candidate "${pkg##*/}"` when brew was absent. That strips the tap prefix, so `steveyegge/beads/bd` became apt package `bd`, which on Ubuntu is an unrelated tool (`bd 1.03-3`). The installed Beads `0.61.0` looked older than apt's `1.03`, the entry was queued as outdated, and the update command then passed the full tap name to `apt-get`, which cannot resolve it.

Beads was removed from `BREW_TOOLS` in db0b00cf2, but the same path still applies to the remaining tap-qualified entry (`max-sixty/worktrunk/wt`) and to any future `owner/tap/formula` entry.

## Change

- `_tool_latest_version`: when brew is absent and the formula is tap-qualified (`*/*`), report `unknown`. No system package manager can upgrade a Homebrew-only tap formula, so no unsatisfiable update is queued.
- `apt` lookup now uses the formula name as-is (identical to before for non-tap names).
- `get_brew_latest`: dropped the now-unreachable `wt` GitHub-release case and tap-stripping; its no-brew branch is only reached by plain formula names.

## Verification

- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/tool-version-check.sh`: clean.
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-tool-version-check-ripgrep.sh`: PASS.
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-tool-version-check-update-failure.sh`: PASS.
- Direct call of `_tool_latest_version brew <pkg> x` with `PATH=/usr/bin:/bin` (apt, no brew), stubbed lookups:

| pkg | before | after |
|-----|--------|-------|
| `steveyegge/beads/bd` | `apt:bd` | `unknown` |
| `max-sixty/worktrunk/wt` | `apt:wt` | `unknown` |
| `jq` | `apt:jq` | `apt:jq` |

## Notes

- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-tool-version-check-classify.sh` fails with `NC: unbound variable` on unmodified `main` as well; it is unrelated to this change and left untouched.
## Regression Evidence

Added `.agents/scripts/tests/test-tool-version-check-tap-formula.sh`. It runs `_tool_latest_version` with a stubbed `PATH` (apt-get only, no brew) and asserts a tap-qualified formula resolves to `unknown`, a plain formula still resolves through apt, and a tap formula still goes to brew when brew is present. Run against `main`'s `tool-version-check.sh` it fails (`expected "unknown", got "apt:bd"`); against this branch it passes.

title: GH#33332: fix(pulse): input_required terminal blocker class with accountable owner
body:
## Summary

Workers blocked on genuinely missing input (for example an unrecorded staging origin) were classified `reason=unknown owner=worker-triage`, stayed `status:available`, and were re-evaluated every pulse cycle under a misleading `dedup_active_claim` reason.

- New terminal-blocker class `input_required`, which requires exactly one `TERMINAL_BLOCKER_INPUT_OWNER=user|contributor|maintainer|admin` line. A missing, invalid or duplicated owner stays `unknown` (retryable). The fingerprint is `v2:input_required:<owner>`, so the public owner comes from an allowlist and never from prose.
- Anti-deferral: the worker contract restricts the class to a specific value, target, credential or decision that is absent from all reachable sources and cannot be derived or safely chosen within delegated authority. Reversible choices, naming, defaults and scope interpretation stay with the AI. The normal known-class lifecycle still applies: the first observation keeps one independent verification attempt, and only a second identical result opens the circuit. The recovery supervisor first decides anything that AI authority covers.
- No new label or review gate. The class reuses the existing circuit hold (`status:blocked`). Its revision tracks the brief and dependencies (like `external_trigger_pending`), so putting the input in the issue body re-arms dispatch.
- The terminal-blocker backoff now classifies as `terminal_blocker_backoff` instead of an active claim. It is benign, and the pulse negative-caches it keyed to `updatedAt`, with a TTL capped at the 15-minute minimum backoff.
- The approval-snapshot canonical release regex accepts `input_required` and the previously missing `external_trigger_pending` writer output. Unlisted owners remain content-bound.

The launch-admissible pulse-check count (issue item 3) remains a separate follow-up, as the review recommended.

title: GH#33373: fix scope-guard false positives on tag-only pushes
body:
## Summary

The pre-push scope guard computed the new-ref baseline as merge-base(HEAD, origin/<default>) using the worktree's checked-out branch instead of the pushed commit. Pushing a tag on origin/main from a task branch behind origin/main therefore diffed from the stale branch point and reported every file merged since then as out of scope. title: GH#33422: docs: private-to-public quality strategy for code repositories
body:
## What

Guidance for code developed privately and launched later as public open source (WordPress plugins and other tools). It comes from setting up CI on a private WordPress plugin repository.

- `.agents/reference/ci-gate-policy.md`: new section "Private repositories and public launch" with two phases.
  - **Private:** the project's own fast CI, all advisory (no branch protection, required checks or paid review apps). Cost controls: only lint on drafts, `concurrency`, caching, short artifact retention. Secure defaults from the start: SHA-pinned actions, read-only tokens, `persist-credentials: false`, no `|| true`.
  - **Public launch:** a full sweep with the free reviewers (CodeRabbit full review, Codacy, SonarQube Cloud, qlty, Socket, CodeQL, secret scanning, Scorecard). Then fix findings by area, shrink baselines and raise strictness, and only then make the core checks required.
- `.agents/workflows/public-launch-checklist.md`: new §9 "Open-sourcing a code repository". It covers visibility approval, a full-history secret scan with rotation, review of issues, PRs, releases, logs and artifacts, licences, `SECURITY.md`/`CONTRIBUTING.md`/templates, app and token least-privilege, and fork-workflow approval.
- `.agents/tools/wordpress/wp-plugin-release.md`: new "Pull Request Quality Gates" table, with the WordPress specifics:
  - WPCS + PHPCompatibilityWP.
  - PHPStan + `szepeviktor/phpstan-wordpress`, including the bootstrap constants, the WP-CLI stubs lag, and the PHPStan `tmpDir` that PHPCS will otherwise tokenize.
  - Release preflight + Plugin Check.
  - A Docker smoke-test pattern: min/latest matrix, every feature on, uninstall leftovers, writing `.htaccess` yourself, and a `debug.log` canary.
  - Dev files excluded from both zips.

These are field-tested: each gotcha listed broke a real CI run or a local check.

title: GH#33484: restore bare slash commands (/full-loop) alongside aidevops- prefix
body:
## Summary

`/full-loop` (along with `/pr-loop`, `/postflight-loop`, `/recall`, `/remember`, `/save-todo` and `/list-todo`) disappeared from OpenCode. Claude Code kept an April-era `full-loop.md` body.

**Root cause**

- Since #18096, `_generate_commands_for_runtime` deploys `scripts/commands/<name>.md` only as `aidevops-<name>`.
- Bare names survived only as stale copies from older generators, so fresh installs never had `/full-loop`.
- #33384 (GH#33355) then pruned unchanged copies of *current* sources at legacy bare names, which deleted the last working `/full-loop`.
- Worker dispatch still sends `/full-loop Implement issue #N` (`pulse-dispatch-lib.sh`, `remote-dispatch-helper.sh`, `deferred-job-helper.sh`), and docs and process matching depend on the bare token.

**Fix** (`.agents/scripts/generate-runtime-config-commands.sh`)

- For OpenCode and Claude Code, deploy every `scripts/commands` source as both `aidevops-<name>` and bare `<name>`.
- Ownership rules for an existing file at a bare name:
  - Identical to the generated output: untouched.
  - Known legacy fingerprint: replaced.
  - Any other regular file: backed up to `~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/backups/commands/<runtime>/` and then replaced.
  - Symlink or non-regular entry: kept, with a warning.
- Names owned by main-agent commands (`.agents/commands`) or hardcoded commands (`agent-review`, `release`, …) are never shadowed.
- `_prune_legacy_commands` skips names that have a live source.
- `generate-runtime-config.sh` parity verification now covers bare aliases, so a stale or missing `/full-loop` invalidates the cache and self-heals.

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-runtime-command-reconciliation.sh`: PASS. Extended to cover the bare alias, user-file backup, stale-alias detection and repair, and no pruning of a legacy-listed name that has a live source.
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-opencode-command-model-tiers.sh`: PASS. Covers the hardcoded-name collision.
- `test-opencode-symlink-cleanup.sh` and `test-agent-discovery-smoke.sh`: PASS.
- ShellCheck is clean on all three changed files.
- Live install: `generate-runtime-config.sh commands --runtime opencode|claude-code`, then `cmp full-loop.md aidevops-full-loop.md` matches in both runtimes, and `verify --runtime opencode` reports a match.

Resolves #33484

title: t18584: fix(pulse): ignore never-terminal 'qlty usage' pending status in merge snapshot
body:
## Summary

Resolves #33495.

The pulse pre-merge snapshot (`_pmrc_snapshot_checks_acceptable` in `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-required-checks.sh`) treated every pending check as active CI. Qlty posts a non-required `qlty usage` commit status ("You have used 90%+ of your analysis minutes this period.") as `pending` and never completes it, so every PR on an affected repository was logged `not ready (active=1, blocking_failures=0, advisory_failures=0)` on every pass and never auto-merged.

Evidence: wpallstars/wp-plugin-starter-template-for-ai-coding #269 and #270 (worker PRs for #262/#263) were green with the review-bot gate passing for 2+ hours; the only non-terminal status on each head was `qlty usage` = pending. Both were then merged through `full-loop-helper.sh merge`, which does not wait on non-required statuses.

## Change

- `PMRC_INFORMATIONAL_PENDING_STATUS_CONTEXTS_JSON` lists known never-terminal informational statuses (currently `qlty usage`).
- A pending check is ignored only if it is a single commit-status context, not required, and in that list. Each ignore is logged. Required contexts, check runs and terminal failures are unchanged.
- The flag is computed in jq and placed beside the name, because `IFS=$'\t' read` collapses the empty conclusion of pending rows and shifts later columns.

## Verification

- `shellcheck -x` on both changed files: clean.
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-preflight-snapshot.sh`: 110 run, 0 failed. Two new cases: non-required pending `qlty usage` passes; the same context as a required check still blocks.
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-required-checks-filter.sh`: passed.

title: GH#33513: fix: materialize criss-cross merge-base blobs for prospective merge guard
body:
## Summary

Root cause: with several merge bases, merge-ort merges them into a virtual base and reads blobs changed between those bases and their own merge bases. The prefetch only enumerated diffs from each top-level merge base, so those blobs were never requested and merge-tree failed closed with 'could not fetch <oid> from promisor remote'. Reproduced identically on Apple Git 2.50.1 and Git 2.53.0, so it is version-independent. Fix: enumerate merge-base pairs recursively (bounded to 32 pairs, fail closed above), keep the single explicit bounded blob fetch, then verify every wanted blob is present with cat-file --batch-check under GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH and block with counts only (no paths/content) if anything is missing.

title: GH#33570: fix(pulse): gate worker admission on CPU pressure
body:
## Summary

Resolves #33570.

- Add one-minute load/logical-core CPU admission (default threshold 1.5).
- Preserve RAM and configured cap limits; running workers are not terminated.
- Recheck pressure on refill and prevent the minimum-worker floor reopening admission.
- Ship configuration defaults, schema, environment mapping and documentation.

## Files and reference pattern

Implementation: `.agents/scripts/pulse-capacity.sh`, `pulse-capacity-alloc.sh`, `pulse-wrapper-config.sh`, and `config-helper.sh`; configuration: `.agents/configs/aidevops.defaults.jsonc`, `aidevops-config.schema.json`; docs: `.agents/reference/configuration.md`. Follow the existing sourced capacity-function and `config_get` patterns. Scoped runtime coverage: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-cpu-admission.sh`.

## Verification

- ShellCheck: all five changed shell files clean.
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-cpu-admission.sh`: 24 assertions pass.
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-wrapper-characterization.sh`: 54 tests pass.
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-wrapper-worker-count.sh`: 42 tests pass. Its existing temporary-HOME fixture emits missing-defaults warnings; no assertions fail.
- `shfmt -d .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-cpu-admission.sh`, JSON schema property check, `git diff --check`, commit/push hooks: pass.

## Runtime Testing

Risk: medium. Testing level: runtime-verified using sourced production calculation and dispatch-capacity functions with stubbed OS/provider inputs. Both Darwin and Linux parsing are exercised, including load/core 41.2/16, equality, RAM/cap limits, unavailable telemetry, malformed configuration, minimum floor, startup and refill. A saturated dispatch reports `0 7 0` (target, active, slots); low pressure restores `20 7 13`. No live workers are killed or production saturation induced; this does not claim a live deployment cycle on the reporting macOS host.

## Decisions

Zero means admission closed, not an invalid capacity file. Above-threshold load closes new admissions, including refill. Invalid thresholds fall back to 1.5; missing telemetry leaves existing limits in force and logs `cpu_gate=unknown`.

## Acceptance self-review

| Criterion | Result | Evidence |
|---|---|---|

title: GH#33569: fix(pulse): skip unchanged no-op in-cycle merge evaluations
body:
## Summary

The in-cycle deterministic_merge_pass re-enriched and re-evaluated the same open PRs every cycle with merged=0 (~560s on a loaded runner), leaving dispatch_max below its 600s per-candidate floor. New sub-library .agents/scripts/pulse-merge-unchanged-skip.sh records a per-repo fingerprint (number, state, draft, head SHA, base, updatedAt, labels) after each complete from-index-0 evaluation with no merge/close/failure and no fail-closed enrichment. _merge_ready_prs_for_repo (.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-process.sh) skips enrichment and per-PR evaluation only for opted-in callers (PULSE_MERGE_UNCHANGED_SKIP=1) when the fingerprint is unchanged, the no-op streak is >=2 (PULSE_MERGE_UNCHANGED_SKIP_MIN_STREAK) and the last full evaluation is younger than PULSE_MERGE_UNCHANGED_SKIP_MAX_AGE_SECONDS (default 1800). Due exact retry targets, paused PR/enrichment cursors, list changes, progress, age expiry or degraded enrichment always force a full evaluation. pulse-wrapper.sh opts the in-cycle pass in and gives it a fixed graceful share (PULSE_MERGE_IN_CYCLE_BUDGET_SECONDS, default 300s; the existing PR cursor resumes next cycle). The standalone merge routine is unchanged and still evaluates every pass. title: GH#33616: perf: reduce serialized dispatch ceremony startup
body:
## Summary

Resolves #33616

Collapse the precheck/claim ceremony into one claim-helper process without removing trust, assignment, consensus, or final ownership gates. Attribute startup, takeover analysis, precheck, and consensus waits separately.

Retain the footprint cache in the dispatch shell instead of losing it in nested command substitutions. Empty snapshots now respect the same 30-second TTL as populated ones. Every candidate still reads and writes atomic reservations under the existing lock.

Read live substantive comments before consolidation's child/ownership/PR ceremony. An ordinary unlabeled issue below the threshold needs only that comment read; issues that might consolidate and labeled cleanup paths retain every existing gate.

### Files

- `.agents/scripts/dispatch-claim-helper.sh`: combined command and latency attribution
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-dedup-layers.sh`: direct combined claim entrypoint
- `.agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-footprint.sh` and `pulse-dispatch-core.sh`: in-process result interfaces retaining the repo cache
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-triage.sh`: avoid unnecessary consolidation-only lookups
- Existing claim, footprint, and consolidation test scripts: focused regression coverage

The canonical issue scope was corrected before adjacent library/test edits, with caller evidence and collision discovery recorded on #33616.

## Safety and decisions

- Use one isolated claim-helper process rather than sourcing its CLI into Pulse: this avoids changing Pulse's shell options or colliding with helper function names while eliminating both dedup forwarding startups and the second claim startup.
- Keep fresh final ownership reads: neither the earlier candidate metadata nor the takeover-only comment snapshot authorizes dispatch after the consensus window.
- Queued assignment is required before spawn by worker ownership checks. Post-launch hooks already follow spawn. These safety-critical paths are deliberately not deferred or made fire-and-forget.
- Consolidation comments are candidate-specific, so they are not cached across issues or used as repository-wide authorization. Only impossible consolidation actions short-circuit.
- Independent static safety review of the exact changed semantics found no actionable introduced defects (moderate confidence).
- The outer `claim_consensus` dispatch stage now covers the combined precheck/claim invocation; the separately attributed `[dispatch-claim]` precheck and consensus records distinguish the components. Do not interpret the outer stage as identical to the older claim-only measurement.

## Verification

- ShellCheck on all 8 changed shell scripts and `git diff --check`: pass. Commit hooks also pass.

title: GH#33619: fix: preserve stdin in timeout_sec macOS fallback
body:
## Summary

Root cause of the prospective TODO merge guard failure ("N of N required prospective blobs were not materialized"): when neither timeout nor gtimeout is on PATH (coreutils-less macOS), timeout_sec backgrounds the command with `set -m; "$@" &`. Inside a subshell Bash has no job control, so the async command gets /dev/null as stdin and the caller redirect is ignored. `_merge_run_bounded_isolated_git` is a subshell, so `git fetch --stdin` received zero blob OIDs, exited 0, and verification correctly failed closed. Fix: an explicit `<&0` on the async command so the fallback passes stdin through exactly like GNU timeout/gtimeout. Merge-guard logic in full-loop-helper-merge.sh is unchanged: `--filter=blob:none` with explicit blob wants is correct (Git promisor lazy-fetch uses the same form), so no `--no-filter` change is needed. Also carries two pre-existing merge-suite isolation fixes from closed fork PR #33632 (co-authored by @aswiler): test-full-loop-merge-authority-guard.sh extracts cmd_pre_merge_gate from full-loop-helper-readiness.sh (4 checks were failing on main), and test-full-loop-merge-body-file.sh stubs _merge_admin_fallback_required_checks_clear (2 checks were failing on main). Behaviour note: in the fallback path, callers that do not redirect stdin now inherit it instead of /dev/null, matching the existing timeout/gtimeout paths on Linux and coreutils hosts.

title: GH#33658: feat(seo): public SERP collection policy, SerpApi provider, CAPTCHA threshold probe
body:
## Summary

Lets aidevops check questionable SERP-provider data against real search results, and measure how much paced collection one browser identity tolerates.

- **Policy** (`.agents/aidevops/reach-capture.md` "Public Search-result Collection"): paced, logged-out SERP collection is allowed from the operator's machine, headed or headless, optionally through a registered residential/ISP/mobile egress profile. Stop at a CAPTCHA/challenge (a human may solve it in a headed session); do not rotate identities to keep going after a block. Automated CAPTCHA solving stays off by default. Aligned wording in `capsolver.md`, `proxy-integration.md`, `anti-detect-browser.md`, `auto-browse.md`, and `reach-failure-lib.sh`.
- **SerpApi provider**: `keyword-research-helper.sh` gains SerpApi for organic results and autocomplete (`SERPAPI_API_KEY` via env, `credentials.sh`, or gopass), plus `serp-compare <keyword>` to diff the top organic results across DataForSEO, Serper, and SerpApi (skips unconfigured providers). Docs: `.agents/seo/serpapi.md`, `keyword-research.md`, `seo.md`, onboarding entries, subagent index.
- **CAPTCHA-threshold probe**: `serp-probe-helper.sh` + `serp-captcha-probe.mjs`. Persistent Playwright profile, typed queries, randomized gaps (default 45–120 s), optional egress profile/proxy secret, report + result HTML saved locally (mode 600). Stops at the first challenge, or waits for a human with `--on-captcha wait`. Never solves CAPTCHAs.
  - Presents as an ordinary browser (`navigator.webdriver` false). With the default automation flags, Google challenged the very first query.
  - `--consent reject` clicks "Reject all" on cookie prompts; `--hidden` (macOS) runs headed but hidden so it doesn't take over a shared screen, and shows the window only when a human must act. Pages still report `visibilityState: visible`.
  - Decodes Google `/url?q=` / opaque `/goto` links (falls back to the displayed cite) and Bing `/ck/a` links.
  - Split into `serp-probe/` modules (`engines.mjs`, `options.mjs`, `session.mjs`, `window.mjs`) so no file trips Qlty `file-complexity`.

## Observed results (one residential connection, Brave, Google UK, direct egress, 2026-10-05)

| Run | Pacing | Outcome |
|---|---|---|
| Automation flags on | 10–15 s | Challenge on query 1 |
| Flags fixed | 45–60 s | 2/2 |
| 30-query run | 45–120 s | 30/30, no challenge (41 min) |
| 100-query run, `--hidden` | 20–40 s | Challenge at query 42 after 41 searches in 27.9 min (~1.5/min) |

Roughly 73 Google searches over ~90 minutes from one IP before the first challenge. This is a per-machine, per-network observation, not a guarantee; the docs say so.

## Verification

- `linters-local.sh --changed --base-ref origin/main`: pass (string-literal ratchet regressions fixed).
- `node --check .agents/scripts/serp-captcha-probe.mjs`; ShellCheck clean on changed shell files.
- `serp-probe-helper.sh plan ...` dry runs report `contacted_targets: false`; invalid proxy URLs, unknown egress profiles, `--on-captcha wait --headless`, and `--hidden --headless` are rejected.
- Parsers checked offline against saved Google/Bing HTML with all network requests aborted.
- After the module split: `qlty smells` reports no smells on the probe and its modules (was `file-complexity` 96). Live hidden Bing run with the persistent profile: 1/1, 6 organic results, `window: hidden`, `webdriver: false`.
- `keyword-research-helper.sh serp-compare "crm software" --locale uk-en --depth 5`: live DataForSEO results; Serper/SerpApi skipped (no keys configured). SerpApi request path is not live-verified.

## Regression Evidence

This is a feature PR; the only platform-specific code is the opt-in macOS `--hidden` mode (`serp-probe/window.mjs`). It needs a logged-in macOS GUI session, `osascript` with AppKit, and a live headed browser, none of which exist on CI runners, so an automated regression test is not possible. It was verified manually on macOS: hidden 100-query and 2-query runs reported `window: hidden`, kept focus on the previous app, and pages reported `visibilityState: visible`. Non-macOS runs reject `--hidden` during option validation (`--hidden is macOS-only`), and the rest of the probe has no platform branches beyond the Meta/Control select-all key.

## Notes

- The policy no longer cites specific rulings in *Google LLC v. SerpApi, LLC*; they could not be verified against a docket during this work. It points readers to the docket instead.
- Known limitation: some Google layouts (for example travel results for "things to do in edinburgh") have no standard organic titles, so the probe records 0 parsed results. That is not counted as a block.
- Observed once: a hidden Bing run with `--fresh-profile` completed 2/2 without a challenge but parsed 0 organic results (HTML not kept); the persistent profile parsed normally. Likely a first-visit Bing page variant; not yet investigated.

Resolves #33658
